bc_funarama_the_nursery.blurb: The Nursery is a compact wall in the Smoke Bluffs area of Squamish, set across the trail from the far left end of the main Funarama crag. It holds seven short routes: six trad lines and one sport line. Most are easy to moderate at a gentle angle, with a single harder sport route, which makes it a friendly place to warm up or to bring someone who is just starting to lead. The wall can also be rigged for top-roping, and a boot path on the left side leads to the top.

bc_runestone_wall.blurb: Runestone Wall is a small, slabby crag in the Smoke Bluffs area of Squamish, a short stroll up the trail from Lower Crag X. Seven routes are described here, six of them trad and one sport, and several can also be top-roped. The grades start with a very easy line, add a few mid-range 5.8s and a single 5.6, and top out with a couple of 5.10s, so newer leaders and people after short crack climbs both find something. The wall picks up sun in the afternoon, and the walk in takes under five minutes.

bc_pink_cliff.blurb: Pink Cliff is a modest little cliff in the Smoke Bluffs area of Squamish. All seven routes are trad, and most carry bolted or chain anchors, so top-roping is an option. The grade spread leans toward 5.10, with four climbs there, plus one 5.6, one 5.7 and one 5.9. The best lines are said to be on the middle slabs. Afternoon sun reaches the face, and the descent is a straightforward walk off to the left. It is a spot with a few fun climbs rather than a busy one.
bc_pink_cliff.approach: From the top of the Penny Lane stairs, go up the gully and past Fern Gully, then follow the trail left; the cliff is the next one on the right.

bc_the_zip_south.blurb: Zip (South) is a small cliff of seven routes in the Smoke Bluffs area of Squamish, reached along the Blind Channel Trail just south of the municipal water pipe. Six lines are trad and one is sport, and the grades sit mostly around 5.10, with a single 5.11 and one 5.12 sport line at the top end. It is not a beginner spot. Expect a handful of well-regarded moderate-to-hard trad climbs, including a standout hand-sized crack, rather than a large collection of routes.

bc_zoe.blurb: Zoe is a compact crag in Murrin Park, on Highway 99 south of Squamish. Seven routes are described, six sport and one trad, with grades from 5.8 through 5.12; the bulk are 5.10s and 5.11s, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate-to-hard sport. The climbing is sustained and technical. The cliffs face so that they are shaded in the afternoon, which helps on hot days. The walk in is short, and a picnic table sits at the base.
